segments.t: On one of those days,
as he was teaching the people in the temple
and preaching the Good News,
segments.note: 「the Good News」は εὐαγγελιζομένου に含まれる目的語を表に出したもの

segments.t: the priests and scribes came to him with the elders.
segments.note: ἐπέστησαν（近づいた）を「came to him」と訳す

segments.t: They asked him,
“Tell us:
by what authority do you do these things?
Or who is giving you this authority?”
He answered them,
“I also will ask you one question.
segments.note: λόγον（一つの問い）を「one question」と訳す

segments.t: Tell me:
the baptism of John, was it from heaven, or from men?”
They reasoned with themselves, saying,
“If we say, ‘From heaven,’
he will say,
‘Why didn’t you believe him?’
But if we say, ‘From men,’
all the people will stone us,
for they are persuaded that John was a prophet.”
They answered that they didn’t know where it was from.
segments.note: μὴ εἰδέναι πόθεν（どこからか知らない）を「didn’t know where it was from」と展開

segments.t: Jesus said to them,
“Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things.”
He began to tell the people this parable:
“A man planted a vineyard
and rented it out to some farmers,
and went into another country for a long time.
segments.note: 「into another country」は ἀπεδήμησεν（旅に出た）の展開

segments.t: At the proper season,
he sent a servant to the farmers
to collect his share of the fruit of the vineyard.
segments.note: δώσουσιν αὐτῷ（彼に与える）を「collect his share」と組み替え

segments.t: But the farmers beat him and sent him away empty.
He sent yet another servant,
and they also beat him
and treated him shamefully,
and sent him away empty.
He sent yet a third,
and they also wounded him and threw him out.
The lord of the vineyard said,
‘What shall I do?
I will send my beloved son.
It may be that
segments.note: ἴσως（おそらく）を「It may be that」と訳す

segments.t: seeing
segments.note: WEB はビザンティン本文に従い「seeing」を補う。ギリシャ語本文にこの語はない

segments.t: him, they will respect him.’
“But when the farmers saw him,
they reasoned among themselves, saying,
‘This is the heir.
Come, let’s kill him,
that the inheritance may be ours.’
Then they threw him out of the vineyard and killed him.
What therefore will the lord of the vineyard do to them?
He will come and destroy these farmers,
and will give the vineyard to others.”
When they heard that, they said,
“May that never be!”
segments.note: Μὴ γένοιτο（あってはならない）を「May that never be」と訳す

segments.t: But he looked at them and said,
“Then what is this that is written,
‘The stone which the builders rejected
was made the chief cornerstone’?
segments.note: εἰς κεφαλὴν γωνίας（隅の頭に）を「the chief cornerstone」と訳す

segments.t: Everyone who falls on that stone will be broken to pieces,
but it will crush whomever it falls on to dust.”
The chief priests and the scribes sought
segments.note: 語順の組み替え（英語は祭司長→律法学者の順）

segments.t: to lay hands on him
that very hour,
but they feared the people—for
they knew he had spoken this parable against them.
They watched him and sent out spies,
who pretended to be righteous,
that they might trap him in something he said,
segments.note: λόγου（言葉）を「something he said」と展開

segments.t: so as to deliver him up to the power and authority of the governor.
They asked him,
“Teacher,
we know that you say and teach what is right,
segments.note: ὀρθῶς（正しく）を「what is right」と名詞化

segments.t: and aren’t partial to anyone,
segments.note: πρόσωπον λαμβάνεις（顔を受ける＝えこひいきする）の意訳

segments.t: but truly teach the way of God.
Is it lawful for us to pay taxes to Caesar, or not?”
segments.note: φόρον（税）を「taxes」と複数化

segments.t: But he perceived their craftiness, and said to them,
“Why do you test me?
segments.note: WEB はビザンティン本文に従い「Why do you test me?」を補う。ギリシャ語本文にこの句はない

segments.t: Show me a denarius.
Whose image and inscription are on it?”
segments.note: 「are on it」は英語の補い

segments.t: They answered, “Caesar’s.”
He said to them,
“Then give to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s,
and to God the things that are God’s.”
They weren’t able to trap him in his words before the people.
segments.note: 「him」「his」は英語の補い

segments.t: They marveled at his answer and were silent.
Some of the Sadducees came to him,
segments.note: αὐτὸν（12番）はギリシャ語では文末だが「came to him」に対応

segments.t: those who deny that there is a resurrection.
segments.note: ἐπηρώτησαν（11番）は英語では次節冒頭に現れるので対応なし

segments.t: They asked him,
segments.note: 「They asked him」は前節の ἐπηρώτησαν αὐτὸν と λέγοντες の組み合わせ

segments.t: “Teacher,
Moses wrote to us that
if a man’s brother dies
having a wife,
and he is childless,
his brother should take the wife
and raise up children for his brother.
segments.note: σπέρμα（子孫）を「children」と訳す

segments.t: There were therefore seven brothers.
The first took a wife, and died childless.
The second
took her as wife, and he died childless.
segments.note: WEB は前節の展開を補う。ギリシャ語本文は「そして第二の」までしかない

segments.t: The third took her,
and likewise the seven all left no children, and died.
Afterward the woman also died.
Therefore in the resurrection whose wife of them will she be?
For the seven had her as a wife.”
Jesus said to them,
“The children of this age marry and are given in marriage.
But those who are considered worthy to attain to that age
and the resurrection from the dead
neither marry nor are given in marriage.
For they can’t die any more,
for they are like the angels
and are children of God,
being children of the resurrection.
But that the dead are raised,
even Moses showed at the bush,
when he called the Lord
‘The God of Abraham,
the God of Isaac,
and the God of Jacob.’
Now he is not the God of the dead, but of the living,
for all are alive to him.”
Some of the scribes answered,
“Teacher, you speak well.”
segments.note: εἶπας（言った）を現在形「speak」と訳す

segments.t: They didn’t dare to ask him any more questions.
segments.note: οὐκέτι は「any more」に、οὐδέν は「questions」に含まれる

segments.t: He said to them,
“Why do they say that the Christ is David’s son?
David himself says in the book of Psalms,
‘The Lord said to my Lord,
“Sit at my right hand,
until I make your enemies the footstool of your feet.”’
“David therefore calls him Lord, so how is he his son?”
In the hearing of all the people,
he said to his disciples,
segments.note: 「his」は英語の補い

segments.t: “Beware of those scribes
who like to walk in long robes,
and love greetings in the marketplaces,
the best seats in the synagogues,
and the best places at feasts;
who devour widows’ houses,
and for a pretense make long prayers.
These will receive greater condemnation.”
